title: Adjunct Instructors - Business and Economics
description:
Under the general direction of the Dean and the Chair of the
Department of Economics and Business Administration (EBA) in the
Delaplaine School of Business and Communication (DSBC) at Hood
College, we invite applications from qualified candidates
interested in serving as Adjunct Faculty in one or more of the
following disciplines:

Accounting, Economics
Entrepreneurship
Finance
General Management
Human Resource Management
International Business
Marketing & Selling
Sports Management.

This advertisement is intended both to address immediate
instructional needs and to develop a pool of qualified adjunct
faculty for future teaching opportunities. Adjunct faculty members
typically teach one or two courses per semester, depending on
departmental needs and instructor availability.

Under the general direction of the Dean of the Delaplaine School of
Business and Communication and the Chair of the Department of
Economics and Business Administration, adjunct faculty will teach
undergraduate and/or MBA courses consistent with their academic
qualifications, professional expertise, and the instructional needs
of the department.

Current priority areas include Finance and Investments, Investment
Analysis, and Sales and Marketing.

The department particularly welcomes applications from accomplished
professionals who are interested in bringing their industry
experience into the classroom, as well as advanced doctoral
candidates seeking to broaden their college-level teaching
experience.

Essential duties include the following. Other duties may be
assigned. Primary responsibilities include:

Teaching assigned undergraduate and/or MBA courses in the
Department of Economics and Business Administration.
Preparing course syllabi, instructional materials, assignments,
assessments, and other course-related materials consistent with
departmental and College expectations.
Providing high-quality instruction that integrates relevant
academic concepts with contemporary professional practices.
Facilitating an engaging, inclusive, and student-centered
learning
Evaluating and assessing student performance and providing
timely and constructive
Maintaining appropriate communication with students and
departmental
Complying with College and departmental academic policies
and
Performing other instructional responsibilities related to
assigned courses as

Qualifications

We seek a candidate who values diversity, equity and inclusion in
all that they do. Candidates must have strong organizational skills
and a proven ability to work collaboratively with partners across
campus in support of Hood College’s mission as a student-centered,
liberal arts institution.

To perform this job successfully, the individual must be able to
perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed
below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability
required.

Education and/or Experience Minimum
Requirements/Qualifications

Candidates should possess appropriate academic and/or professional
qualifications in the discipline in which they will teach.

Preferred qualifications include:

A doctoral degree in business, economics, or an appropriate
business-related discipline, such as accounting, finance,
management, marketing, or human resource management; or
A master's degree or MBA in an appropriate discipline combined
with significant relevant professional experience.

For accounting and finance, relevant professional credentials are
highly valued. These may include credentials such as: Certified
Public Accountant (CPA), Certified Management Accountant (CMA), and
Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA).

All academic degrees must have been awarded by an appropriately
accredited institution of higher education.

Preferred Skills and Characteristics

College- or university-level teaching experience is preferred.
Prior teaching experience at Hood College is also considered an
asset. The department will additionally consider applicants with
substantial professional or industry expertise who demonstrate the
ability to translate that experience effectively into undergraduate
or graduate instruction.

Technology Skills

Proficient in MS Office tools (Microsoft Word, Excel, and
PowerPoint), e-mail and Internet. Ability to learn new applications
quickly including organization-wide information systems and
department-specific software applications.

Language Skills

Strong oral and written communication skills. Ability to
effectively provide information and positively respond to questions
from both external and internal customers both in person and by
phone. Ability to author routine reports and correspondence.

Mathematical Skills

Proficient with statistical and financial concepts. Must have the
ability to apply those concepts to tracking, projections, goal
setting, and interpreting reports. Must be able to draw conclusions
from reports and make cost effective decisions regarding
programs.

Reasoning Ability

Ability to solve practical problems and deal with a number of
concrete variables in situations where only limited standardization
exists. Ability to interpret a variety of instructions furnished in
written, oral, diagram, or schedule form. Ability to work
independently and as a member of a group in developing and
executing project plans. Ability to work in the theoretical arena
and apply logic as appropriate.

Physical Demands

The physical demands described here are representative of those
that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the
essential functions of this job. While performing the duties of
this job, the employee is frequently required to stand; walk; use
fingers, hands, reach with hands and arms; and talk and hear. The
employee is required to sit. The employee may occasionally be
required to stand and lift and move up to twenty-five pounds.
Specific vision abilities required include close vision. Reasonable
accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities
to perform essential functions.

Work Environment

The work environment described here is representative of what an
employee will encounter while performing the essential functions of
this job. The noise level is usually moderate and could include
interaction with other employees, students, the public, telephones,
and other office equipment.

Compensation

Salary range is from $1075/credit for undergraduate courses and
$1215/credit for graduate courses. These temporary positions are
not benefits-eligible except for participation in Hood’s Group
Supplemental Retirement Annuity (GSRA) plan and paid Maryland sick
leave. Learn more about Hood College .

To Apply

We invite qualified candidates to apply online via our electronic
application which requires submission of a cover letter, resumé and
three professional references.

If you need assistance with the online application process, please
email humanresources@hood.edu or call (301)
696-3592.
